events.title: Zhu Di takes the Ming throne as the Yongle Emperor
events.description: Zhu Di, fourth son of the dynasty's founder, the Hongwu Emperor, became the third Ming emperor, having seized the throne from his nephew. He later moved the capital to Beijing and began building the Forbidden City.
events.html: Zhu Di, fourth son of the dynasty's founder, the Hongwu Emperor, became the third Ming emperor, having seized the throne from his nephew. He later moved the capital to Beijing and began building the Forbidden City.

events.title: Charles VII is crowned king of France at Reims
events.description: Charles VII, king of France since 1422, was crowned in Reims Cathedral, the traditional place of French coronations, after Joan of Arc had raised the siege of Orléans. He went on to recover northern France and Gascony from the English.

events.title: French artillery wins the Battle of Castillon
events.description: French cannon cut down an English army under John Talbot at Castillon in Gascony. It was the last battle of the Hundred Years' War, leaving Calais as England's only possession in France.
events.html: French cannon cut down an English army under John Talbot at Castillon in Gascony. It was the last battle of the Hundred Years' War, leaving Calais as England's only possession in France.

events.title: Deposed Tsar Peter III dies in captivity
events.description: Days after his wife Catherine seized the throne in a coup, Peter III died at Ropsha, almost certainly murdered by her supporters. Catherine the Great went on to rule Russia for 34 years.
events.html: Days after his wife Catherine seized the throne in a coup, Peter III died at Ropsha, almost certainly murdered by her supporters. Catherine the Great went on to rule Russia for 34 years.

events.title: Bolsheviks execute the Romanov family in Yekaterinburg
events.description: In the early hours, Nicholas II, his wife, their five children and four retainers were shot in the cellar of the Ipatiev House. Their remains were found decades later; the Orthodox Church canonised the family in 2000.
events.html: In the early hours, Nicholas II, his wife, their five children and four retainers were shot in the cellar of the Ipatiev House. Their remains were found decades later; the Orthodox Church canonised the family in 2000.

events.title: The Potsdam Conference opens
events.description: Truman, Stalin and Churchill, later replaced by Attlee, met at Cecilienhof near Berlin. They settled the occupation of Germany and issued the Potsdam Declaration demanding Japan's unconditional surrender.
events.html: Truman, Stalin and Churchill, later replaced by Attlee, met at Cecilienhof near Berlin. They settled the occupation of Germany and issued the Potsdam Declaration demanding Japan's unconditional surrender.

events.title: American and Soviet spacecraft dock in orbit
events.description: An Apollo capsule docked with Soyuz 19, and Thomas Stafford and Alexei Leonov shook hands through the hatch. The first international crewed space mission was a landmark of Cold War détente.
events.html: An Apollo capsule docked with Soyuz 19, and Thomas Stafford and Alexei Leonov shook hands through the hatch. The first international crewed space mission was a landmark of Cold War détente.

events.title: TWA Flight 800 explodes off Long Island
events.description: A Boeing 747 bound for Paris exploded minutes after take-off from New York, killing all 230 on board. Investigators concluded that a spark had ignited fuel vapour in the centre wing tank.
